findings.title: Socket connecting during authorization can miss a committed message
findings.evidence: The handler captures getWebSockets() at line 151, awaits external D1 authorization at 159, commits only at 184-188, and broadcasts exclusively to the captured peers at 191. fetch() can accept a new socket and send its snapshot at 60-75 during that external await. Such a snapshot precedes the commit and lacks the message, while the new socket is absent from the saved peer array and misses its event. The comment at 197 does not change the fixed recipient array.
findings.impact: A connected authorized client can miss a live message until reconnect, violating message-to-every-connected-member and coherent snapshot/live delivery behavior.

findings.title: Broadcast ignores expired recipient authorization leases

contract.requirement: Phase-one socket authorization may use a bounded lease of at most five minutes, capped by the actual session expiry.

findings.evidence: src/teams.ts:9 sets LEASE_MS=4*60*1000, and :184-189 sets expiresAt=min(session.expires_at*1000, Date.now()+LEASE_MS) in server-created x-room-expires. src/room.ts:43 saves that deadline in the attachment. The sender checks its own deadline at :52-53 and fetch() evicts expired peers at :33-38, but broadcast at :73-75 sends unconditionally to every attached peer. There is no recipient deadline/current authority check on that path.
findings.impact: A socket connected earlier can continue receiving protected messages after its lease or actual session expires while a later-connected authorized sender remains active. It is only cleaned up if it sends a message or another handshake occurs.
